analysis:
The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is a documentation addition of about 35 lines (head lines 3541-3575): a new section, "Cluster service listeners follow the cable and the pairing". The supplied units are base-side text from later in the file (lines 4495-5336), so they contain none of the changed lines. I examined that text for context. It covers GPT-OSS/MiMo/Qwen batch ownership, TP request charges, the Qwen media ingress, and cluster runtime facts. None of it is altered by the PR.

The documented behavior is a periodic (5 s) listener check that restarts the setup-exchange and control-lease listeners when the cable port or address changes or the pairing changes. It stops them when no pairing exists, and it ignores an unreadable pairing store. Pairing identity compares both pins, the cluster label, the link epoch and the edge, but never the edge secret. Stale listeners refuse handshakes keyed with a later pairing (`handshakeRejected`). That is a fail-closed behavior, and it does not weaken any trust boundary. I found no threat-model regression, authorization bypass, data exposure or change to attestation custody in this documentation-only diff.

Open question for the next pass: the source files behind the new text (ClusterService.swift `listenerChange`, `ensureResponder`, `ensureControl`, and ClusterSetupLinkExchange pairing identity) are not in the supplied units, and the patch excerpt is truncated. Behavior cannot be confirmed against code. Two details are worth checking if code changes ship alongside: (1) whether the pairing identity comparison that excludes the edge secret could leave a listener keyed with a stale secret after the secret rotates, and (2) whether silent restarts and stops of the control-lease listener affect auditability. Neither is evidenced as a regression here.
